messages:
kevin: Heads-up — quick spike idea. Instead of per-tenant peering or long-lived private endpoints, what if we push a tiny managed control-plane sidecar into customer VPCs that only proxies control/config traffic to our global control plane? Pros/cons?

lina: Do you mean a light-weight relay that only handles auth + config sync and keeps no long-term state? Sounds like a sidecar but intentionally minimal.

samir: Major win is avoiding cross-account peering and complex route tables. Big concern: egress IPs — many customers still require stable source IPs for allowlists.

anya: Operational cost question: running sidecars across thousands of customer VPCs vs a few regional relays. How do we handle upgrades/rollbacks safely? Canary? auto-rollback?

kevin: Sketch of the contract: sidecar runs in customer VPC, listens on 127.0.0.1:15001, accepts local connections (agent or control plane SDK), establishes mTLS to our controlplane. Sidecar is stateless: config is pushed, and it routes requests. Fallback policy: if sidecar can't reach controlplane, route via regional relay (if customer enabled).

samir: NAT/IP preservation: if sidecar initiates outbound to our control plane, customers that need a fixed egress IP might still need a small NAT appliance we manage or a peering option. We can offer an optional egress appliance (managed EC2/NLB pair) per customer.

lina: Security surface: keys in the sidecar are sensitive. Can we avoid persisting long-lived keys? Use short-lived tokens fetched from the customer's KMS or an STS flow so sidecar stores nothing persistent. Also consider hardware-backed keys where possible.

anya: From a compliance/enterprise perspective, this starts to look like Private deployment. Customers will ask about logs/metrics — do they want those sent to us or kept local? Need to be explicit.

kevin: Prototype config (rough):
```yaml
sidecar:
  listen: 127.0.0.1:15001
  controlplane_endpoint: cp-prod.redwood.net:443
  auth: sts
  token_ttl: 5m
  nat_mode: none # options: none | managed-egress | peering
  fallback: regional-relay
```
This lets us toggle nat_mode per customer and keep sidecar small.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: branch sidecar-proxy-spike deployed to staging. CI: https://ci.internal/build/1234 :rocket:

samir: Quick staging numbers: handshake median ~20ms eu-west, cpu negligible for 1k simulated tenants. Throughput good up to 500 agents per sidecar instance; need a 5k scale test to be confident.

lina: Next steps I suggest: 1) enumerate failure modes (connectivity, token refresh failures, compromise scenarios), 2) draft minimal ACLs and network requirements for customers, 3) security review checklist. I'm happy to own the failure-mode doc.

kevin: I'll write a 1-pager for sales/solutions that describes options (sidecar-only, sidecar+managed-egress, peering). Will link into RFC follow-up. Thanks all :thumbsup:
